chunks: Hadith 1487 — Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the takbir in the two Eids, and he said: “They are twelve: seven in the first and five in the other. When you stand for the prayer, say one takbir, then say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. O Allah, You are the Lord of majesty and greatness, and the Lord of generosity, might, power, authority, and honor. I ask You on this day which You have made an Eid for the Muslims, and for Muhammad—may Your blessings be upon him and his family—a ذخْر and increase, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and that You send blessings upon Your near angels and Your sent prophets, and that You forgive us and all believing men and believing women, and Muslim men and Muslim women, the living among them and the dead. O Allah, I ask You from the good of what Your sent servants asked You for, and I seek refuge in You from the evil from which Your devoted servants sought refuge.”

Allah is greater, the first of everything and its last, the originator of everything and its final end, knowing every thing and its return; the destination of every thing is to Him and its return is to Him; and He is the manager of affairs and the raiser of...

the accepter of deeds, the bringer forth of hidden things, the discloser of secrets. Allah is greater, tremendous in dominion, intense in might, living and never dying, everlasting and never passing away.
“When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: Be, and it is.”

Allah is greater. Voices are humbled before You, faces submit before You, sights are bewildered before You, and tongues grow weary from describing Your greatness. All forelocks are in Your hand, and the measures of all affairs belong to You; none judges concerning them other than You, and nothing of them is completed without You. Allah is greater. Your preservation encompasses every thing, Your might subdues every thing, Your command penetrates every thing, and every thing stands by You. Every thing humbles itself before Your greatness, is abased before Your honor, surrenders to Your power, and yields before Your sovereignty. Allah is greater. And you recite al-Hamd and...
“By the sun and its morning brightness”

and you bow with the seventh. And in the second, you say: Allah is greater, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. O Allah, You are the Lord of majesty and greatness. You complete all of it as you said at the beginning of the takbir. This statement is said in every takbir until you complete five takbirs. And the khutbah in the two Eids is after the prayer.

ai.seo_question: How many takbirs are in the Eid prayer, and what is recited between them according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the structure of the Eid prayer takbirs: seven in the first rak'ah and five in the second, along with the supplication recited between them. It also includes expressions of tawhid, praise of Allah, seeking blessings upon Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ, forgiveness for the believers, and states that the Eid khutbah is delivered after the prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1487 – Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as):

I asked him about the Takbir (saying "Allahu Akbar") in the Eid prayers.
Imam (as) said: "There are twelve Takbirs: seven in the first Rak'ah and five in the second. When you stand for the prayer, say the first Takbir, then recite:
'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. O’ Allah (swt), You are the One worthy of majesty and greatness, the One worthy of generosity and authority, of power and sovereignty, and of honor. I ask You on this day, which You have made an Eid for the Muslims and a treasure and increase for Muhammad, to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to send blessings upon Your close angels and Your sent prophets. Forgive us, all believing men and women, and all Muslim men and women, the living among them and the dead. O’ Allah (swt), I ask You for the best of what Your chosen servants have asked You for, and I seek refuge with You from the worst of what Your sincere servants sought refuge from.

Allahu Akbar, the first of all things and their last, the originator of all things and their end, the knower of all things and their return, the one to whom all things belong and are directed. You are the One who directs all matters, raises the dead,

unveils hidden matters, and reveals secrets.
Allahu Akbar, the greatness of the dominion belongs to Him, the might of the power is His, the Living who never dies, the Eternal who never ceases to exist.
When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.

Allahu Akbar, before whom all voices become silent, all faces bow in humility, all sights are bewildered, and all tongues fall short of expressing His greatness. Every forelock is in His hand, and the measure of all matters is in His control. None decrees except Him, and nothing is fulfilled except through Him.
Allahu Akbar, His preservation encompasses all things, His might overcomes all things, His command prevails over all things, and all things are established by Him. Everything humbles itself before His greatness, surrenders to His might, submits to His power, and yields to His sovereignty.
Then you recite Surah Al-Hamd (Al-Fatiha) and 'Wa al-Shams wa Duhaaha' (Surah Ash-Shams).

You perform the Ruku after the seventh Takbir. In the second Rak'ah, you repeat the Takbir and say:
'Allahu Akbar, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah (swt), alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. O’ Allah (swt), You are worthy of majesty and greatness.'
You continue in this way for each Takbir until you complete the five Takbirs. The khutbah (sermon) for the Eid prayers is delivered after the prayer."
